home.headline: Components that compile straight to Vapor, not around it.
home.tagline: A Vue 3 UI library with a real Vue Vapor build.
home.featureVaporTitle: Real Vapor build, not a shim
home.featureVaporBody: Every component compiles through Vue 3.6's Vapor mode from the same source.
home.featureAnimationBody: Plain CSS by default, or drive it yourself with GSAP or motion-v.
home.featureI18nBody: Every built-in string translates through your own i18n instance.
home.featurePrimitivesBody: No compound-component sprawl, no hidden context to wire up.
home.featureSsrBody: Every component checks for a real browser before touching window or document, so it renders safely in Nuxt, server-rendered apps, and static site generators. This documentation site is built with Vite SSG using the same components.
home.featureSkillBody: A companion package that teaches Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and other agents every component's real API, generated from the library's own types, not hand-written.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.intro: A Vue 3 component library with a full Vue Vapor build and an animation-agnostic design: plain CSS by default, or bring your own animation library.
gettingStarted.vaporIntro: Both builds ship from the same package and source. Pick whichever your app runs, or mix both (Vue 3.6 supports VDOM/Vapor interop). Every component page has the same toggle to compare them.
gettingStarted.installIntro: vael-ui is published on npm. Install it with whichever package manager you use:
gettingStarted.usageImportNote: Every component brings its own styles now. Only needed if you're on a version before 0.2.0, or want everything loaded at once. See {link} for base-style setup.
gettingStarted.usageIntro: Then use any component: from 'vael-ui' for the classic VDOM build, or 'vael-ui/vapor' for the compiled Vapor build (Vue 3.6's no-virtual-DOM mode). Same props either way:
gettingStarted.darkModeIntro: CSS-only: responds to <html data-theme="dark">, falling back to prefers-color-scheme. No toggle UI shipped; useColorScheme() handles persistence and OS-preference updates:
gettingStarted.directivesIntro: v-tooltip and v-scroll-mask aren't global by default. If you use either in more than one component, register them once:
gettingStarted.directivesNote: v-tooltip also needs a <TooltipHost /> mounted once. In a Vapor app, import both directives from vael-ui/vapor instead.

globalSetup.title: Global setup
globalSetup.intro: Four singletons. Mount each once, anywhere in your app, and every other component reaches it automatically.
globalSetup.tooltipHostIntro: Powers every v-tooltip. Without one mounted, tooltips silently never appear.
globalSetup.tooltipHostOptions: It takes the same options every individual tooltip can override:
globalSetup.dialogHostIntro: Renders whatever openDialog() or confirmAction() creates imperatively. Not needed for a <Dialog v-model:open> in your own template. No props, no configuration.
globalSetup.popoverHostIntro: Renders whatever openPopover() or confirmAction() with surface: 'popover' creates imperatively. Not needed for a <Popover v-model:open> in your own template. No props, no configuration.
globalSetup.toasterIntro: Renders whatever {code} creates. Has real configuration, so it keeps {link}.
globalSetup.allTogetherIntro: Mount all four once, wherever your app's root template lives:

tailwind.layerNote: vael-ui ships in {layer}. Tailwind v4 wraps its own utilities in a layer too, so order matters: import vael-ui's CSS before your Tailwind entry (below) so its layer registers first, keeping Tailwind's utilities layer after it in the cascade. A Tailwind utility on a vael-ui component then always wins, no {important}, no specificity fights. See {link} for the general mechanics.
tailwind.orderWarning: Most consumers no longer need an explicit vael-ui/style.css import since 0.2.0 — each component loads its own CSS automatically. Tailwind v4 is the exception: its utilities live in their own cascade layer, and whichever stylesheet registers a layer name first wins the ordering. Import vael-ui's CSS before your Tailwind entry, in your app's main entry file, so this holds even as more components' CSS loads later.
tailwind.mergingIntro: Every component accepts a ui prop for part classes (e.g. :ui="{'{'} root: 'my-class' {'}'}"). To resolve conflicting Tailwind utilities there the way tailwind-merge would (last one wins per property), wire it up once:
tailwind.mergingNote: Every ui.* part class in the tree now passes through twMerge.

stylingLayers.title: Styling and cascade layers
stylingLayers.intro: vael-ui ships in {layer}. Unlayered CSS always wins over a layer regardless of specificity, so a plain, unlayered base reset silently overrides vael-ui internals. Fix: put your base styles in a layer too, ordered first.
stylingLayers.orderNote: That's it. Import order here only controls layer position, nothing else, an unlayered override anywhere always still wins regardless of load order.
stylingLayers.bundlerNote: Every component brings its own styles now. Only needed if you're on a version before 0.2.0, or want everything loaded at once.
stylingLayers.overrideNote: Deliberately overriding one component ({code} prop, a Tailwind utility) wants your rule to win, keep that CSS unlayered as it already is by default. See {link}.
stylingLayers.cssVariablesIntro: Every color, radius, shadow, and motion value in vael-ui reads from a CSS custom property. Override any of them in your own unlayered stylesheet:
stylingLayers.cssVariablesThemeNote: ConfigProvider's theme prop covers primary, danger, and radius for dynamic, JS-driven theming. Everything else here is CSS-only.

rows.primary: Primary action color (buttons, links, focus accents).
rows.primaryHover: Hover state for the primary color.
rows.primaryContrast: Text/icon color on top of the primary color.
rows.contrastVariant: Text/icon color on top of this color.
rows.surface: Base background for panels, cards, and dialogs.
rows.borderStrong: Stronger border color for emphasized edges.
rows.overlay: Backdrop color behind modals and dialogs.
rows.radius: Base corner radius for controls (buttons, inputs, badges).
rows.radiusSurface: Capped corner radius for large surfaces (panels, cards, tables), so an aggressive radius choice can't turn them into a stadium shape.
rows.zPopover: Stacking order for popovers, menus, and selects.
rows.toastOffset: Edge offset for the toast stack.

animation.title: Bring your own animation
animation.intro: Every component that animates ships a plain CSS transition, but exposes a real escape hatch to drive it with GSAP, motion-v, or nothing at all. Check a component's own Props/Slots/Exposed tables for which of these it has, not every component has all three.
animation.motionCssIntro: false disables the built-in CSS transition, the component still changes state instantly, leaving the DOM ready for you to animate.
animation.forceMountIntro: Keeps content mounted while closed instead of removing it on v-if. Pair with <AnimatePresence> and the default slot's isClosing flag to own exit timing yourself.
animation.beforeCloseIntro: For imperative libraries: pass a function that receives done. The component stays mounted and isClosing until you call it.
animation.motionVExampleIntro: forceMount plus the default slot's isClosing flag, wrapped in <AnimatePresence>:
animation.gsapExampleIntro: beforeClose(done) plus the exposed panelEl ref, so the tween runs on the real panel element before it's removed:

descriptions.ConfigProvider: Wraps your app to provide theming, i18n, and class-merging to every component below it.
descriptions.Button: A clickable action with variants, sizes, loading states, and icon slots built in.
descriptions.SplitButton: A primary action fused with a chevron that opens alternate actions in a dropdown.
descriptions.Toolbar: A horizontal strip for grouping related actions, with roving keyboard focus.
descriptions.SpeedDial: A floating action button that fans out into secondary actions on demand.
descriptions.Dial: A circular drag control for picking a numeric value, like a volume knob.
descriptions.SelectButton: A segmented control for choosing one (or several) values from a short list.
descriptions.Input: A single-line text field with sizes, states, and slots for icons or hints.
descriptions.Textarea: A multi-line text field that can auto-grow with its content.
descriptions.InputNumber: A numeric field with increment/decrement controls and format-aware parsing.
descriptions.OtpInput: A row of single-character boxes for one-time codes, with paste and auto-advance.
descriptions.PasswordInput: A password field with a reveal toggle and a requirements hint.
descriptions.Checkbox: A tri-state toggle for a single yes/no/indeterminate choice.
descriptions.Radio: One option in a mutually-exclusive set, always used inside a RadioGroup.
descriptions.RadioGroup: Coordinates a set of Radio buttons so only one can be selected at a time.
descriptions.Switch: An on/off toggle styled like a physical switch, for immediate-effect settings.
descriptions.Slider: Drag a handle (or two, for a range) along a track to pick a numeric value.
descriptions.Knob: A rotary control for picking a numeric value within a fixed arc.
descriptions.Field: Wraps a form control with a label, help text, and error message, wired together for you.
descriptions.DatePicker: A text field paired with a calendar popover for picking a date or range.
descriptions.Calendar: A month grid for picking a single date, multiple dates, or a range.
descriptions.FileUpload: A drop zone and file list for picking files, with validation and progress.
descriptions.Select: A dropdown for picking one or more values from a list, with search and virtualization.
descriptions.Combobox: A searchable dropdown that also accepts free text, so autocomplete and tagging are one component.
descriptions.CascadeSelect: A dropdown for picking a path through nested options, one level at a time.
descriptions.Tree: A collapsible, indented list for hierarchical data with single or multi-selection.
descriptions.TreeSelect: A dropdown whose panel is a Tree, for picking one or more nodes from a hierarchy.
descriptions.Dialog: A modal overlay that interrupts the page until the user responds or dismisses it.
descriptions.Drawer: A panel that slides in from a viewport edge, for navigation or side content.
descriptions.Popover: A floating panel anchored to a trigger element, for menus, forms, or extra detail.
descriptions.Tooltip: A small floating label that appears on hover or focus to explain an element.
descriptions.BottomSheet: A panel that slides up from the bottom edge, common on touch layouts.
descriptions.ContextMenu: A menu that opens at the pointer on right-click, replacing the native browser menu.
descriptions.Tour: A guided walkthrough that spotlights one element at a time behind a positioned callout, for onboarding and product tours.
descriptions.Menu: A dropdown list of actions opened from a trigger, with full keyboard navigation.
descriptions.MenuList: The same row rendering as Menu, but always in-flow, built for a permanent sidebar nav.
descriptions.Tabs: Switches between panels of content, with a sliding indicator under the active tab.
descriptions.Toaster: Renders the notifications created by toast(). Mount it once, anywhere in your app.
descriptions.Message: An inline banner for status text: info, success, warning, or error.
descriptions.Progress: A bar or ring showing completion of a determinate or indeterminate task.
descriptions.Loader: A small spinner for indicating that something is in progress.
descriptions.Skeleton: A placeholder shape that mimics real content while it is still loading.
descriptions.DataTable: A data grid with sorting, selection, resizing, and virtualization, composed from Columns.
descriptions.Column: Defines one column of a DataTable, always used inside its tree.
descriptions.Pagination: Page-number controls for splitting a long list or table across pages.
descriptions.Card: A bordered container for grouping related content, with optional title and actions.
descriptions.Avatar: A circular (or square) image or initials, representing a person or entity.
descriptions.Badge: A small dot, count, or label overlaid on the corner of another element.
descriptions.Tag: A compact label for categorizing or annotating an item inline.
descriptions.Chip: A removable, compact token for selected filters, tags, or multi-select values.
descriptions.Kbd: Styles a keyboard shortcut so it reads like a physical key.
descriptions.Accordion: A stack of collapsible sections where opening one can close the others.
descriptions.AccordionItem: One collapsible section of an Accordion, always used inside its tree.
descriptions.Collapsible: A single show/hide section for content that is optional or secondary.
descriptions.Separator: A thin line (or gap) for dividing content into visually distinct groups.
descriptions.Resizable: A draggable handle for letting the user resize a panel between a min and max size.
descriptions.SwipeToReveal: Swipe an item to reveal actions underneath it, like a native mobile list row.
descriptions.Sortable: A drag-to-reorder list with a real keyboard path, not just a pointer one.
descriptions.PullToRefresh: A pull-down gesture at the top of a scroll container that triggers a refresh.
descriptions.Dock: A macOS-style row of icons that magnify as the pointer approaches them.

autoImport.title: Auto Import
autoImport.intro: vael-ui/resolver is a resolver for unplugin-vue-components — register it once and every vael-ui component becomes usable in a template with no manual import at all.
autoImport.setupIntro: Add the resolver wherever unplugin-vue-components is already configured:
autoImport.setupOutro: That's it — write the tag, the import gets inserted at build time:
autoImport.vaporIntro: vael-ui ships two builds from the same source: the regular VDOM build and a Vapor build (vael-ui/vapor). By default the resolver imports from the VDOM build; pass variant: 'vapor' to resolve from the Vapor build instead. Pick whichever your app actually renders with — mixing the two in one app isn't supported.
autoImport.oneImportIntro: If your editor's auto-import keeps suggesting vael-ui instead of vael-ui/vapor — a known TypeScript limitation when a package exports the same name from two entry points — set a vapor export condition instead of importing from the subpath. Every import … from 'vael-ui' then resolves to the Vapor build project-wide, components and composables alike, and there's nothing left for auto-import to pick wrong.
autoImport.oneImportNote: The Vite condition controls what actually loads; the TS condition just keeps types matching it. Set one without the other and you'll get a silent mismatch — correct types with the wrong build loaded, or vice versa — not an error.
autoImport.cssIntro: No extra wiring needed here. Every vael-ui component already imports its own CSS internally, so resolving the component import pulls its styles in for free — unlike most unplugin-vue-components resolvers, which need a separate sideEffects entry to also import a component's stylesheet.
autoImport.bundlersIntro: unplugin-vue-components supports Vite, Webpack, Rollup, esbuild, and Rspack. The resolver itself is just a plain function — it works identically regardless of which one you use.

nuxt.title: Nuxt
nuxt.intro: vael-ui/nuxt is a Nuxt module — add it once and every vael-ui component becomes usable in a template with no manual import at all, using Nuxt's own built-in component registration instead of unplugin-vue-components.
nuxt.setupIntro: Register the module in your Nuxt config:
nuxt.setupOutro: That's it — write the tag, Nuxt resolves the import for you:
nuxt.excludeIntro: Skip specific component names — useful if you want to register your own <Button> under that same tag instead:
nuxt.vdomOnlyIntro: This module always registers from the regular vael-ui build, never vael-ui/vapor — so there's no variant option here the way vael-ui/resolver has one. Vue 3.6 itself supports Vapor SSR hydration, but the stable Nuxt release has no Vapor configuration yet — it's landing behind specific upstream PRs, not yet in a general release. Once Nuxt's own Vapor support ships, a variant option can follow.
nuxt.resolverIntro: If your Nuxt setup already drives component auto-import through unplugin-vue-components for other libraries, use vael-ui/resolver instead — see the {link} guide.

skill.title: AI Agent Skill
skill.intro: A companion package that teaches AI coding agents, including Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Cursor, how to actually use vael-ui: every component's real props/slots/events, every composable, and how to wire up animation, theming, and the vdom/vapor split. Generated straight from the library's own types and docs content, not hand-written, so it stays accurate as the library evolves. Versioned and released independently of vael-ui itself.

composableDescriptions.confirmAction: An async-aware confirm flow, centered as a dialog or anchored to a trigger as a popover, that awaits your handler before closing.
composableDescriptions.useDialogService: Opens any component as a dialog from code instead of markup, resolving a promise with whatever it closes with.
composableDescriptions.usePopoverService: Opens any component as an anchored popover from code instead of markup, resolving a promise with whatever it closes with.
composableDescriptions.useToast: Imperative toast notifications from anywhere in your app, with variant shortcuts and a promise-aware loading-to-success/error swap.
composableDescriptions.useTour: The headless state machine behind Tour: step and group navigation, with zero DOM or rendering baked in.
composableDescriptions.useAsyncLoading: Tracks every in-flight promise passed to it, so a loading state clears only once all of them have settled.
composableDescriptions.useNumberFormat: Locale-aware number formatting and parsing kept in sync, so typed text and its formatted display always agree.
composableDescriptions.useColorScheme: Drives light, dark, or system theme mode from one composable, with persistence left up to you.
composableDescriptions.useFloatingPosition: The Floating UI-backed positioning engine behind Popover, Menu, and Tooltip, for building custom anchored surfaces.
composableDescriptions.useVirtualizer: Windowed rendering for long lists, so only the visible rows exist in the DOM.
composableDescriptions.useFieldControl: Wires a custom form control into the nearest Field: id, ARIA attributes, and focus or filled state.
